title: Trust evidence can be silently replaced at an existing destination

scenario.observed_change: Attestation publication permits an existing destination and later replaces it, so a previously established external trust artifact can be silently clobbered or raced by another creator.
mutable_state: existence and identity of the destination entry
bytes of the previously established trust artifact
authority_boundaries: new operation-owned trust evidence versus pre-existing external trust evidence
preflight observation versus publication-time namespace state
operation_model: publish by replacement at the requested name

required_invariants.requirement: A destination-state decision must remain valid through publication and must not silently act on a different or concurrently created effective target.
The operation must distinguish its owned state from pre-existing or concurrently created state rather than overwrite or remove the latter without authorization.

must_investigate: concurrent creation between preflight and publication
must_identify: replacement publication can destroy previously established trust evidence and make later verification trust newly substituted bytes
must_not_claim: safe trust-root publication merely because the existing file itself is read-only

provenance.note: GitHub Copilot review identified that the attestation destination could overwrite an arbitrary existing external file via replacement publication; the repair changed the artifact to create-once/no-clobber publication.
